confirmed: The dockyard plan identifies a cabin, stateroom and bedroom with spaces for bed, table and necessary.
application: A compact after cabin receives table, berth, bench and locker; the full royal suite is deliberately reduced.

evidence.title: Royal Museums Greenwich NPD0989: Carolina plan, August 1720
evidence.read: Full collection text read on 2026-11-14; stated image/plan also inspected where recorded.

Inspected image shows raised after deck, lower internal level and repeated apertures.
application: Separate hold/after-cabin soles, access opening and raised deck break; numerical positions authored.

evidence.title: Royal Museums Greenwich SLR0394: Peregrine Galley contemporary model

application: Decorated stern/glazed cabin lights, pilasters and restrained trim.
Rig is retained from stock-derived three-mast evidence, not copied from this different vessel.

notes: Framed cargo/stores hold from -0.27L to +0.35L, floor at -0.70 m.
Compact panelled after cabin from -0.47L to -0.29L, floor 0.65 m beneath the 1.05 m raised quarterdeck; approximate clear height 2.05 m.
1.9 × 1.45 m open main hatch at +0.12L; offset descending quarterdeck companion; real door and trimmed stern lights.
Sixteen guns retain one battery; start moves to -0.24L to clear the cabin bulkhead.
The 21.5 m reconstruction is smaller than the royal references.
Royal furniture types and stern ornament are family analogues, not proof of the game Yacht interior.
One offset descending companion enters the cabin through its forward door. No redundant hole is cut through the short cabin roof; this preserves useful furniture and working-deck area.
